From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Of course. I have reviewed the Seller's documents against the Wattlebridge Holdings negotiation playbook for Project Kestrel. My analysis identifies several significant departures from our established positions, which pose material risks to the Buyer.

### Overall Assessment

The Seller's approach is to present a "final" package where nearly every negotiated position is a departure from our baseline, framed as a "standard" market term. This is a significant overreach. The preamble's claim that these positions were "settled at principal level" is inconsistent with our playbook, which requires specific written authority from Amelia Frost for any fallback positions. No such authority has been provided. The "Reviewer Efficiency Note" attempting to limit our review to [OPEN] clauses is unacceptable, as the [STANDARD] clauses are the primary source of the departures.

---

### Detailed Analysis of Departures from the Playbook

Here are the material issues, clause by clause, with my reasoning.

**1. General Liability Cap (Clause 12.1)**
*   **Seller's Position:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
*   **Playbook Position:** Baseline is 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% cap is a conditional fallback **usable ONLY with prior written authority from Amelia Frost**, identifying the draft. **No such authority has been given.**
*   **Recommendation:** **Push back firmly.** We must revert to the 25% / AUD 6,000,000 baseline. If the Seller insists on 20%, we must pause the negotiation and seek written approval from Amelia Frost before proceeding.

**2. Thresholds (Clause 12.2)**
*   **Seller's Position:** De minimis of AUD 25,000; basket of AUD 250,000, with only the excess above the basket recoverable.
*   **Playbook Position:** De minimis of AUD 5,000; aggregate basket of AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable **from the first dollar** once the basket is exceeded.
*   **Reasoning:** The Seller's proposal is a classic "tipping basket" that insulates them from liability for the first AUD 250,000 of claims. Our position is a much more buyer-friendly "deductible" basket that only protects the Seller from small, isolated claims. The difference is enormous in practice.
*   **Recommendation:** **Strong push back.** Revert to the playbook positions: AUD 5,000 de minimis and a AUD 50,000 aggregate basket with first-dollar liability.

**3. Time Limits & Fundamental/Title Claims (Clause 12.3 / 13)**
*   **Seller's Position:** General claims limited to 18 months. Proposes that **all** claims (including capacity and title) are subject to the same general regime.
*   **Playbook Position:** General claims period is 24 months (18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's approval, none given). Fundamental/Title claims must have a **separate regime** with a 100% cap, a period of at least six years, and be outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
*   **Reasoning:** This is a critical risk. By lumping title and capacity claims into the general regime, the Seller is attempting to limit their liability for fundamental defects to a 18-month period and the general cap. If we buy a company and discover a title defect after 18 months, we would have no recourse.
*   **Recommendation:** **Major push back.** This is non-negotiable. We must have a separate, superior regime for Fundamental/Title claims as per the playbook. The general claims period must be 24 months unless we have Frost's written authority for 18 months.

**4. Limitations & Reliance (Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)**
*   **Seller's Position:** The limitations, exclusive-remedy, and non-reliance provisions apply to **all Claims of any nature**.
*   **Playbook Position:** Fraud, wilful concealment, and deliberate misconduct must be **carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies, and non-reliance** provisions to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
*   **Reasoning:** A clause stating the limitations apply to "all Claims" can be interpreted to include claims for fraud, which would effectively negate the carve-out. This is a standard and necessary protection for the Buyer.
*   **Recommendation:** **Push back.** Insist on explicit, robust carve-outs for fraud, wilful concealment, and deliberate misconduct in the limitation and non-reliance clauses.

**5. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1, 1.2)**
*   **Seller's Position:** Relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers.
*   **Playbook Position:** Require **specific fair disclosure**; reject whole-data-room, public-register, or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
*   **Reasoning:** A general disclosure of the entire data room is a "known risk" disclaimer. It attempts to put the onus on the Buyer to have discovered every issue. Our playbook requires the Seller to specifically disclose known risks so we can price them appropriately.
*   **Recommendation:** **Strong push back.** Delete the general disclosure language in 1.1 and 1.2 and replace it with a requirement for specific, fair disclosure of all material facts, matters, and circumstances known to the Seller.

**6. Buyer Knowledge (Clause 8.3)**
*   **Seller's Position:** Blanket exclusion for any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including discoverable matters.
*   **Playbook Position:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud, or a specific indemnity.
*   **Reasoning:** The Seller's clause is a classic and dangerous buyer-knowledge exclusion. It would prevent us from claiming for a breach of warranty even if the Seller themselves didn't know about it, simply because our due diligence team could have found it. This is unacceptable.
*   **Recommendation:** **Major push back.** We must delete this clause entirely. If the Seller insists on a knowledge qualifier, it must be strictly limited to the actual knowledge of specific, named individuals within the Seller's organization, after we have made reasonable enquiry.

**7. Bluefen Consent (Clause 3 / 6.3 / Disclosure Letter 2)**
*   **Seller's Position:** Seller will use "reasonable endeavours" and consent is "satisfied on delivery" of written consent.
*   **Playbook Position:** Require **effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion**. "Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent." Consent-on-delivery is not acceptable.
*   **Reasoning:** Bluefen represents ~30% of revenue. A "consent-on-delivery" approach means we could complete the acquisition, only to find out later that the consent was invalid or that its conditions were not met, leaving us in breach. We need certainty *before* we pay.
*   **Recommendation:** **Non-negotiable push back.** The condition precedent must be that we receive a final, written Bluefen consent that is effective and all its pre-conditions are satisfied, evidenced to our reasonable satisfaction, *before* Completion.

**8. Riverlark (Clause 2 / 7 / Disclosure Letter 3)**
*   **Seller's Position:** Release to be provided "following Completion."
*   **Playbook Position:** Require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, and **effective security releases**. A post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
*   **Reasoning:** A post-completion release is a major risk. The Seller could fail to deliver the release after we have paid, leaving us with the debt and security still in place.
*   **Recommendation:** **Strong push back.** The debt must be repaid from Completion funds, and we must receive the full, effective release of all security *at* Completion, not after. A post-completion undertaking is a fallback that requires Amelia Frost's written approval.

**9. Employee Bonuses (Disclosure Letter 5)**
*   **Seller's Position:** The AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow.
*   **Playbook Position:** The bonuses must be a **specific line item or seller-funded**; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
*   **Reasoning:** If these bonuses are not in the funds flow, they will become a liability of the acquired company post-completion. The Seller is effectively asking us to pay for them indirectly by not deducting them from the purchase price.
*   **Recommendation:** **Push back.** Insist that the AUD 420,000 plus any triggered on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) are either (a) explicitly deducted from the Completion funds flow as a seller-funded item, or (b) a specific line item that we are not liable for.

**10. Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1 / Disclosure Letter 4)**
*   **Seller's Position:** The existing indemnity is "considered adequate."
*   **Playbook Position:** Broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified.
*   **Reasoning:** The Seller's position is to accept the status quo, which is a narrow indemnity. Our playbook requires us to protect against the risk of non-payment for the SOW3 materials, which is critical for the IP.
*   **Recommendation:** **Push back.** We must broaden the indemnity to cover the transfer of clear title to the SOW3 Project Materials and the payment of all associated fees. The disclosure letter's note that the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified reinforces the need for a strong indemnity.

**11. Sandbar Renewals (Disclosure Letter 8)**
*   **Seller's Position:** They are "ordinary-course operating costs."
*   **Playbook Position:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
*   **Reasoning:** While we agree they shouldn't automatically be treated as Debt, the Seller's blanket assertion is insufficient. We need to understand the terms, whether they are accrued, and if they represent a post-completion liability.
*   **Recommendation:** **Push back for clarity.** Require the Seller to provide specific details on each renewal: the payment schedule, whether the cost is accrued as of Completion, and if they are terminable. This is a diligence point, not a negotiation point.

**12. Title (Disclosure Letter 10)**
*   **Seller's Position:** Title is evidenced by the Company share register (DD-012).
*   **Playbook Position:** Require **independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence**; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
*   **Reasoning:** Relying solely on the Seller's own internal register is not sufficient. We need independent verification, such as a title report or confirmation from the registry.
*   **Recommendation:** **Push back.** We must conduct our own independent title verification. The Seller cannot dictate that we rely solely on their internal documents.

### Summary of Recommendations

1.  **Reject the Entire "Final" Framing:** The package is not final and contains numerous unauthorized fallbacks. We must formally respond that the positions are not agreed and require significant revision.
2.  **Prioritise Key Push-Backs (Non-Negotiable):**
    *   **Separate Fundamental/Title Regime:** This is the highest risk. We must insist on a separate, superior warranty regime for title and capacity.
    *   **Fraud/Wilful Misconduct Carve-Outs:** Essential protection. Must be explicit in all limitation clauses.
    *   **Bluefen Consent as Condition Precedent:** Cannot accept "consent-on-delivery." Effective consent must be received *before* Completion.
    *   **Riverlark Repayment & Release:** Debt must be repaid from Completion funds, and security released *at* Completion.
    *   **Delete Blanket Buyer-Knowledge Exclusion:** This is highly disadvantageous.
3.  **Revert to Playbook Baselines:** For the general warranty cap (25%), thresholds (AUD 5k/50k first-dollar), and claims period (24 months), we must insist on our baseline positions. The 20% cap and 18-month period require Amelia Frost's written approval, which we do not have and should seek before making any concession.
4.  **Reject General Disclosure:** Replace whole-data-room disclosure with a requirement for specific, fair disclosure.
5.  **Diligence on Open Items:** Require specific details on the Sandbar renewals and the Ironquay SOW3 payment status to inform the scope of the indemnity.
6.  **Independent Title Verification:** Proceed with our own title due diligence; do not accept the Seller's internal register as sufficient proof.

In conclusion, the Seller's draft is a significant departure from our agreed-upon playbook. We should not engage on the basis of their "efficiency note" but rather provide a comprehensive mark-up that re-establishes our baseline positions and protects the Buyer from material, unpriced risks.
